itens.descricao_en: Stop That Shit（别再造史了）｜面向 Codex/GPT 场景的多平台 Hook + Skill Guard：拦截 AI coding agent 无需求的哈希、校验和与任务范围膨胀。 A multi-platform Hook + Skill Guard for AI coding agents in Codex/GPT workflows: stop unrequested hashes, checksums, and task-scope creep.
itens.readme:
Stop That Shit（别再造史了） 
   把活干完。把多余的停下。 
   正式版 0.2.6  — 用 Skill、Guard 和 STSS，帮助 AI 完成当前任务，删去没有用途的额外工作和防御性文字。 
  Codex · Claude Code · OpenCode · Hermes Agent CLI · Pi · Oh My Pi 
   SHIT 哲学  ·
   看个例子  ·
   安装  ·
   案例库  ·
   English  ·
   한국어 
---
你只让 Agent 导出一个文件，它顺手算了份没人读取的 SHA-256，说是“以防万一”。
你让它 Review，它找到问题就开始改。你让它修一个点，它又想重构旁边的模块。检查已经回答了当前问题，它还想再拉一个 Agent，“最后确认一下”。
理由一个比一个严谨。东西还没交付，token 已经花了一截，你还得盯着它，别让任务继续跑偏。
**活还没拿到，我先当上了 Agent 的监工。**
我也试过往 `AGENTS.md` 里补规则：“不要乱改”“别过度设计”“没让我做的先别做”。每气一次就补一条，写着写着，`AGENTS.md` 自己也开始造史了。
**Stop That Shit。别再造史了。** 该干的干完整，没用的别往上堆。
## SHIT 是哪四种
我们把这些行为叫作 SHIT：
- **S — Scope creep，范围膨胀。** 修一个问题，顺手重构无关模块。必要的调用方、数据迁移和测试要一起处理；没有当前用途的扩展就停下。
- **H — Hashing & hypothetical hardening，无用防御。** 没人读取的 checksum、为想象中的未来搭的兼容层。防御要能发现问题，并触发拒绝、恢复或诊断。有效的保留，无用的省掉，吞错报成功或制造重复副作用的修好。
- **I — Intent violation，意图越界。** 说了只读 Review，文件还是被改了。审查就报告问题，修改需要授权。用户划的边界必须算数。
- **T — Task thrashing，任务打转。** 没有新问题或变化，读过、测过、审过的又来一遍。能回答当前问题的证据就复用；代码或验收条件变了，再补相关验证。做完、验证充分，就结束。
**把当前责任承担完整，让复杂度随真实需要增长。** 需要多改几个文件、补齐迁移或跑跨组件测试，就做完整。
## 前后对比
下游只读取 `report.csv`，没有发布校验，摘要也没有其他用途。导出逻辑却写成了这样：
```js
await writeFile("report.csv", csv);
await writeFile("report.csv.sha256", createHash("sha256").update(csv).digest("hex"));
```
按 STS 的判断，保留：
```js
await writeFile("report.csv", csv);
```
这个简化示例省掉了无用校验和，文件照常交付。更多场景见[案例库](cases/README_CN.md)。
如果发布流程会读取 checksum，并在不一致时拒绝使用文件，就保留，用 `hash=allow` 放行。
**必要的工作要做全。** 修复配置迁移时，旧数据已经发布且仍需支持，就把迁移、读写双方和兼容性测试一起补齐。哪怕 diff 更大，也不能留下坏掉的调用方。

itens.descricao_en: An embedded local, agent-native graph database supporting Cypher 25 written in Rust. Memory or transactional filesystem.
itens.readme:
# Relate
**A graph database in a single binary — query it in Cypher, embed it anywhere, deploy nothing.**
Relate is an embedded, in-memory property-graph engine written in Rust, with a
CLI for interactive and scripted queries. A graph is a single `.rl` file, a
(markdown) folder, or pure in-memory — durable through a fsync'd write-ahead
log and Parquet checkpoints.
The same engine powers the `relate` CLI, a Python package, Node.js and browser
(WASM) npm packages, a Rust crate, and an optional one-process server speaking
Bolt, HTTP, and MCP. No server to babysit, no infrastructure to operate.
📖 **Documentation: [relatedb.ai](https://relatedb.ai/)** — tutorials, guides,
and the CLI / Cypher / Rust / C API references. The deep references live in
[`docs/`](docs/) in this repository, and the honest list of what Relate does
not do is [`docs/limitations.md`](docs/limitations.md). Several entries there
are deliberate scope, not missing features: the working set fits in memory,
one graph per store, a single user or agent per process — Relate is not a
larger-than-memory warehouse, an analytics engine, or a multi-tenant server.
## Install
**macOS & Linux:**
```bash
curl -sSfL https://relatedb.ai/install.sh | bash
relate skill install    # optional: teach your AI coding agents to drive relate
```
If `relate` is not found afterwards, add `~/.local/bin` to your `PATH` — the
installer prints the line to use.
**Windows (PowerShell):**
```powershell
irm https://relatedb.ai/install.ps1 | iex
re

itens.descricao_en: MCP server and CLI that lets AI agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) see and control Android phones and iPhones. Reads the screen as text. Asks before it pays.
itens.readme:
Give your AI agent a phone. 
  6.9x fewer tokens than mobile-mcp.  
   phonedriver.dev  ·  Docs  ·  Compare  ·  Reference  ·  Benchmarks  ·  Releases 
  English  ·  简体中文  ·  日本語  ·  한국어  
phonedriver gives an AI agent the controls of a phone, an Android phone or an iPhone, real or virtual. It reads the screen, taps a button, and reports what changed, and it asks you before it taps Pay. Use it through MCP with Claude Code, Codex or Cursor, or from the command line. The 6.9x is the token total on [nine phone jobs](#fewer-tokens).
Ask it to test your signup form. Change a setting buried three screens deep. Find the step where your app stops working.
  One real Claude Code session on an Android emulator, ordering on dominos.co.uk: 6.5 minutes at 15x, with the approval prompt at real speed. Nothing was ordered.  Full video (MP4) .  
## Start
```sh
npx -y phonedriver init
```
This adds phonedriver to the agents it finds on your machine: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code and Gemini CLI. It then checks adb, Xcode and your devices and says what to fix. An agent that already has it is left alone; `--dry-run` shows what it would do.
Start an Android emulator or the iOS Simulator, or plug in an Android phone with USB debugging on. With nothing connected, the error names what phonedriver can start, and `phonedriver boot "iPhone 17"` starts it. Then give your agent a job that only a phone can do:
> Open my app and test signup. Try invalid inputs. Report each bug with steps to reproduce i

itens.descricao_en: Your own team of AI bots in one self-hosted binary: spaces, every account you have, handoffs, approvals and routines. Open-source, self-hosted alternative to Grok Bot, Claude Duet and OpenAI dots. Rust + React.
itens.readme:
Your own team of AI bots that check each other’s work before saying “done”. 
   Website  ·
   Docs  ·
   Features  ·
   Compare  ·
   Changelog  ·
   Discussions 
   macOS: one app for Apple silicon and Intel · Linux x86_64 (beta): .deb or AppImage · A server:  binary or Docker  · Phone:  add it to your Home Screen  ·  All downloads  
   Free and open source. A ⭐ helps others find kwant. 
  kwant has no token.  Official X account is  @kwantbot . 
kwant gives you a team of bots that share chats, hand work to each other with an @mention and get it done on their own, on a schedule or while you're away. Each message goes to the bot that fits, and the reply says why. Work shows up as cards on a Mission board, and a task turns **Verified** only when kwant runs the check itself, never on a bot's word. Keep separate spaces for work and home, each with its own bots and accounts. Run it as an app on your Mac, Linux or Windows (beta) PC, or on a server, with the Claude, Codex or Grok CLI you already use, or your own API keys.
It's written in Rust (Tokio, Axum, SQLite) with a React web app embedded in the binary.
